definition: Manifold means many and of many different kinds; varied.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word manifold. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know manifold should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her objections to the merger were manifold, running from the price to the timing to the fate of the night shift.
Several is a modest handful — three or four — nowhere near manifold.
Numerous goes further than several, piling up the count, but it stops short of manifold, which adds that the many things are of many different kinds.

Assorted means of mixed kinds gathered casually together — assorted chocolates, assorted screws in a jar; it is a grab-bag word for physical collections. Manifold is formal and abstract, describing reasons, uses, or objections that are both many and varied. A drawer holds assorted odds and ends; a treaty has manifold consequences.

Myriad means so many that counting them is hopeless — the myriad stars over a desert — and it speaks only to number. Manifold makes a double claim: many, and of many different kinds, even for a set small enough to count. Ten thousand identical bolts are myriad; five unlike reasons are manifold.

The historian's card file gives manifold answers: debts in Ohio, drought in Texas, a brother already out there, a newspaper's promise of free quarter-sections, and, on one card, simply 'tired of fences.' No two wagons rolled west for quite the same reason.
Manifold is more exact than 'numerous' because it counts kinds as well as heads: many and of many different varieties.
Fifty identical complaints would be numerous; fifty different ones are manifold.
The word is formal and a little stately — the everyday phrase is 'all kinds of.'

Manifold suits formal prose — reports, sermons, ceremony: 'the benefits are manifold.' In this unit, keep it apart from multifaceted: manifold describes many varied things (reasons, uses, objections), while multifaceted describes one thing with many sides.
For everyday speech, 'all kinds of' does the same work.
